message.content:
**Quick‑start: Kill VS Code from a Windows command prompt**

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
```

* `/IM code.exe` – target the executable name (`code.exe` is the VS Code process).
* `/F` – force‑terminate (no graceful shutdown).

---

### If you have several VS Code windows or want to kill child processes

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

* `/T` – also terminates any child processes that were spawned by `code.exe` (e.g., extensions, terminals).

---

### Kill a specific instance by PID

1. Find the PID:

   ```cmd
   tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
   ```

2. Kill that PID:

   ```cmd
   taskkill /PID 12345 /F
   ```

---

### Filter by user (useful on a multi‑user machine)

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /FI "USERNAME eq YourUserName" /F
```

---

### PowerShell alternative

```powershell
Get-Process code | Stop-Process -Force
```

---

### Things to keep in mind

| What it does | Why you might want it | Caution |
|--------------|-----------------------|---------|
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` | Quickly close all VS Code windows when the UI is unresponsive | Unsaved work will be lost |
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` | Ensures no orphaned child processes remain | Same unsaved‑work warning |
| `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` | Target a single instance (useful if you only want to close one window) | Make sure you’re killing the right PID |
| PowerShell `Stop-Process` | Works inside PowerShell scripts or ISE | Same unsaved‑work warning |

---

#### Quick cheat‑sheet

| Command | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F` | Force‑kill all VS Code processes |
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` | Force‑kill all VS Code processes + children |
| `taskkill /PID 12345 /F` | Force‑kill a specific process ID |
| `taskkill /IM code.exe /FI "USERNAME eq <user>" /F` | Kill only your own VS Code instances |
| `Get-Process code | Stop-Process -Force` | PowerShell equivalent |

Use the command that best matches your situation. Happy hacking!
